summary.intent: Continue improving monokl, a fast CLI that returns a few ranked code blocks for a question. This turn the user asked about adopting the oxc type checker (tsrs), then asked to keep going on the work, which meant speed, budget accuracy, evaluation and design.
summary.outcome: Advised against adopting tsrs now and recorded it as a watch item. Corrected the 'declaration in output' metric (59/59 after, 15/59 before) and pushed the corrections. Profiled search time and launched a four-track workflow: perf, budget, eval and a read-only design memo. The snippet branch still has no GitHub PR.

repo: monokl runs as a fresh process of about 50 ms per search. Heavy analysis such as type checking belongs in the daemon-style design the spec already reserved.
The spec plans an `oxc_semantic` upgrade for within-file, scope-aware lookup. A cross-file type checker like tsrs would come after that.
The project's non-goals avoid depending on experimental tools.
Benchmark on the zustand checkout: the declaration is in the top 3 for 56 of 59 identifiers, and its line appears in the output for 59 of 59 after the snippet change.
Timing split: a search with no match takes about 7 ms, and one matching 2 files takes about 45 ms. The extra ~40 ms is tied to the match path, and the cause is not yet known.
A decision log and `ARCHITECTURE.md` are maintained centrally. Agents return decision-log text and the lead merges it, to avoid conflicts.
Work is organised as branches and Entire trails. Agents push and run `entire trail create` instead of `gh pr create`.
workflow: An evaluation metric that matches the declaration text must tolerate the `export ` prefix and the trailing brace that signatures drop. Otherwise it undercounts, and the figures need correcting in the decision record.
Measure the baseline with the same corrected metric before comparing before and after.
Split parallel agent work by file ownership, with one branch per track and stacked branches where work depends on the snippet branch.
Cap agent reports at about 200 words and have the lead re-run checks instead of using a separate verifier agent.
Only builder agents write code. A design agent can be read-only and produce a memo with one recommendation and one rejected alternative.
Narrow a performance regression by timing startup, no-match and matching cases, then per subdirectory, then per file.

friction: Entire has not opened a GitHub PR for `feat/search-snippets`, so CI has not run on it, and it is unclear how Entire creates the PR from a trail change.
The earlier 'declaration in output' metric was wrong and produced incorrect figures (47 and 4), which had to be corrected in the decision record and trail.
Knowledge of tsrs is secondhand: it comes from docs and a news article, and it has not been run or checked as a library versus a CLI.
open_items: Find out how Entire opens a GitHub PR from a trail change, so CI can run on `feat/search-snippets` and the new branches.
Add tsrs to the research notes as a watch item. Revisit it when building a type-aware command, and look into the crate and API if the user wants.
Perf track: find why a matching search costs about 40 ms more than a no-match one, and fix it only if outputs stay byte-identical.
Budget track: make `--max-tokens` and `--max-bytes` count the printed output, snippets included.
Eval track: build a standard-library-only scorer for multi-call concept questions against what rg needs to narrow them.
Design track: write a member-level block memo (methods, hooks inside components) with an order of work in 3 or fewer PRs.
Housekeeping: clean up stale worktrees and old trails, and re-check each agent's result as it lands.
